item.title: Riyadh airport evacuated after reported fresh attack, say officials
item.description: King Khalid International Airport has been targeted multiple times this week, with three Saudi civilians including a pilot killed on Thursday ...
item.dc:creator: AP
item.content:encoded: Two regional officials say the airport in the Saudi capital has been attacked again.One official said the Riyadh airport has been evacuated, and the other said air traffic has stopped. They spoke on condition of anonymity because they weren't authorised to speak to the media.King Khalid International Airport has been targeted multiple times this week, with three Saudi civilians including a pilot killed on Thursday.Iran-backed Houthi rebels in neighbouring Yemen have claimed responsibility for those attacks. There was no immediate Houthi statement Saturday.The airport issued a terse alert telling passengers to check with airlines to confirm flights before going there.Fighting in Yemen between the Houthis and the Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces has escalated, with a Saudi-led coalition providing air support for government forces in an attempt to reverse recent Houthi gains along the Red Sea.

'Zelenskyy failed to make a deal': Trump says Ukraine needs new president Speaking at the White House Saturday, Trump said, "I suggest they get a new leader who can make a deal,"adding that "for some reason (Zelenskyy) never does"

Donald Trump and Volodymyr Zelenskyy (Photo: Reuters)

AP Washington 1 min read Last Updated : Oct 10 2026 | 10:46 PM IST

Listen to This Article

US President Donald Trump says it's time for Ukraine to get a new president, suggesting current Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has not done enough to end huis country's war with Russia. Speaking at the White House Saturday, Trump said, "I suggest they get a new leader who can make a deal,"adding that "for some reason (Zelenskyy) never does". Trump also suggested that if he had been US president in 2022, "that war would have never started. There was no reason that that war with Ukraine and Russia started. It started due to incompetence."   Zelenskyy has "lost 30% of your country and you've had over a million people go between the two of them, over 2 million people killed. That's a war that should have never started. And I think it's time for Ukraine to get a new president.

Neither Putin nor Trump wanted to hang up first, says Kremlin aide The Kremlin said most of the conversation focused on efforts to resolve the war in Ukraine. Putin also downplayed the likelihood of three-way peace talks resuming soon

Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump (File Photo: White House)

Reuters 2 min read Last Updated : Oct 10 2026 | 8:33 PM IST

A conversation on Friday between President Vladimir ??Putin and US President Donald Trump was "very substantive and friendly" and neither leader wanted to be the first to end ??the call, Russian news agency Interfax quoted a Kremlin aide as saying.   During the call, the presidents agreed that Russia would supply diesel to the US and global markets to lower fuel prices, prompting an unexpected temporary easing of US sanctions on Russian fuel that has dismayed Ukraine.   The Kremlin said most of the conversation focused on efforts to resolve the war in Ukraine. Putin also downplayed the likelihood of three-way peace talks resuming soon.

Interfax cited Kremlin foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov on Saturday as saying the conversation lasted an hour and a half.   "Neither wanted to be the first to hang up," he said. "They hung up simultaneously, literally at the same time." Also Read

Kyiv is relying on US support in negotiations to end the war. After news of the call broke on Friday, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy condemned the diesel deal in unusually blunt terms, calling it a "weak decision" ??and "an investment in a war that must be ended."   The West imposed sanctions, including restrictions on Russian energy imports, after Moscow launched the full-scale war in Ukraine in February 2022. Efforts to end the fighting have so far stalled, partly over Russia's demand for four Ukrainian regions it does not fully control.

On Friday, negotiators from the US, Ukraine and European countries held talks in Miami aimed at reaching agreement on a unified peace proposal in the coming weeks that could be presented to Russia, according to a person familiar with the discussions.   (Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)     More From This Section

item.title: Anthropic's Claude AI carried out unintended actions on US govt websites
item.description: Anthropic disclosed 4 types of unintended AI behaviour, including exploiting software flaws, submitting unauthorised forms and bypassing access restrictions ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: By Shirin Ghaffary Anthropic PBC said its Claude AI model carried out additional unintended actions on the digital systems of outside organisations, including some US government agencies’ websites, prompting a warning from the Trump administration for artificial intelligence companies to secure their systems. In a report outlining previously undisclosed incidents, Anthropic listed four types of unintended behaviors that the AI has demonstrated, including exploiting basic flaws in software to run commands, submitting forms it should not have and bypassing restrictions to access certain public data. The company said that some of the cases involved websites run by government agencies at the federal, state and local levels, without specifying the agencies. The report did not name the outside entities involved, which Anthropic said was at the request of some of the affected parties.  Anthropic and its rival, OpenAI, have disclosed a spate of incidents in recent months involving their AI models acting in unintended ways, ranging from behaviours like those described in Friday’s report, to hacks of third-party websites. These disclosures have fueled concerns about the security risks of cutting-edge AI. Anthropic said in the report that it sees the behavior as less severe than some other previous incidents involving its AI. “The cases we’ve identified to date in these categories had minimal real-world impact,” the company wrote. In one example of the improper behavior it found, Anthropic said Friday that its Claude Haiku 4.5 model submitted a tip to a local police department about a homicide, stating in the form, “I may have information regarding this case,” and “I recall seeing someone matching the description in the area,” without filling in the site’s name and contact fields. The Philadelphia Police Department disclosed the incident this morning in a press release, the company said. Anthropic also said it briefed the White House on these cases and notified each agency involved. On Friday, Trump administration officials said they were now requiring that AI companies notify affected parties and address security incidents involving their models. “Earlier today, Anthropic contacted the SI Force to disclose the details of various prior incidents that it discovered in late September involving the unauthorised and fraudulent use of government and other systems,” the White House said in a statement from the Super Intelligence Force, a new government unit tasked by President Donald Trump with overseeing AI development and safety.  “The company informed us that these events occurred in the past, the activity has ceased, and there is no ongoing similar activity,” the statement said. Axios reported on the government requirement earlier.  As a result of these uncovered incidents, Anthropic said Friday that it has restricted some types of internet access for its AI models during the testing phase of its training process.
